overview: PGG Wrightson is New Zealand's second-largest rural services company, providing farm inputs retailing (Rural Supplies, Fruitfed Supplies, Water & Irrigation, Agritrade wholesale) and agency services (Livestock, Wool, Real Estate) to New Zealand farmers and growers. Following the May 2019 sale of its PGG Wrightson Seeds business to Denmark's DLF Seeds for roughly NZ$333 million, PGW is now a pure-play rural services business operating exclusively within New Zealand, organised into two reporting segments: Retail & Water and Agency. The company reported FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) operating revenue of $1,074 million -- the first time above $1 billion since the seeds divestment -- Operating EBITDA of $64.3 million and NPAT of $15.6 million.

business_model.summary: PGW earns money through two distinct models: (1) principal retail sales of farm inputs (agrichemicals, animal health, fertiliser-adjacent products, irrigation equipment) at a gross margin through its Rural Supplies, Fruitfed Supplies and Agritrade channels, and (2) commission/agency income from facilitating livestock, wool and real estate transactions where PGW does not take title to the underlying asset. A smaller but distinctive revenue stream is interest income on GO-STOCK, a deferred-payment livestock financing product where PGW retains legal title to stock as security. Retail revenue is transactional and highly seasonal (working capital builds in H1, unwinds in H2); Agency commission revenue is directly linked to livestock/wool/property prices and transaction volumes, making it the most cyclical and highest-operating-leverage part of the business.

revenue_streams.name: Retail & Water (Rural Supplies, Fruitfed Supplies, Agritrade, Irrigation)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2C hybrid -- predominantly individual farmers, graziers, orchardists and viticulturists (SMB-scale rural businesses) purchasing on trade credit terms of up to 12 months; also large corporate/iwi farming entities
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand -- the Group operates and derives revenue exclusively within New Zealand (post-seeds divestment, which removed the only material offshore/multi-geography exposure)

main_competitors: Alliance Group (livestock/meat processor with own procurement)
competitive_position.market_position: Clear #2 in New Zealand rural retail behind Farmlands, which is roughly double PGW's rural retail revenue and operates a 56,000+ member co-operative model; PGW is a leading, and in several categories the largest, player in livestock agency, rural real estate and wool broking, and holds a strong position in horticultural inputs via Fruitfed Supplies

moat_factors.description: Nationwide store and saleyard footprint (Rural Supplies, Fruitfed, livestock agents) built over 175 years gives reach that is costly to replicate, though Farmlands' co-operative network is larger
Long-standing trusted advisor relationships (agronomists, livestock agents) and technical service depth (e.g. Fruitfed's horticultural advisory) support customer retention despite price competition

GO-STOCK livestock deferred-payment product and the Max Rewards loyalty programme create switching costs and data-driven customer insight; livestock agency benefits from established buyer-seller and processor relationships (headage supply-chain partnerships)

moat_factors.factor: Vertical integration into animal health manufacturing
moat_factors.description: FY2026 acquisition of Nexan Group (animal health manufacturer) and launch of the Blue Ag private-label agrichemical range give some cost/margin control and price-point differentiation versus pure distributors
Localised sales relationships and saleyard infrastructure (PGW invests in perimeter/animal welfare/safety systems) are difficult for new entrants to match quickly

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus Farmlands in rural retail, structurally limiting pricing power and buying leverage
Wool remains structurally challenged (a shrinking global synthetic-competing market) despite a cyclical pricing bounce
Commission-based agency income is exposed to margin compression when livestock prices are high (farmers negotiate lower rates/flat headage fees), so revenue and margin can move in opposite directions
Thin net margins (NPAT margin ~1.5% in FY2026) leave limited buffer against a commodity downturn or cost inflation
Concentrated, contested shareholder register (Agria ~44%, Elders ~12%) creates governance overhang and board instability risk rather than a clean strategic partnership

growth_drivers: Cyclical recovery in farmgate returns: strong sheep/beef schedules, elevated cattle prices, and a supportive Fonterra milk price are driving on-farm confidence, input spend and livestock transaction volumes
Nexan Group acquisition (FY2026) vertically integrates animal health manufacturing, expanding Agritrade's offering and margin capture
Blue Ag private-label agrichemical range launched in FY2026 -- improves supply resilience, price-point control and gross margin versus third-party brands
bidr online livestock bidding/livestreaming platform expanding saleyard integration (16 saleyards) -- digital channel for the Livestock agency business
Rural real estate recovery as lower interest rates and improved dairy/sheep-beef profitability reactivate buyer interest, particularly for dairy and finishing properties
GO-STOCK receivables at record highs, reflecting growing farmer demand for PGW's deferred-payment livestock financing product
R&D expansion (Hastings research station lease) supporting horticultural/agricultural trial capability and technical differentiation
Continued store network modernisation (new-format Rural Supplies/Fruitfed sites) improving customer experience and operating efficiency

business.description: Earnings are directly geared to farmgate milk price, sheep/beef schedules, wool prices and rural property transaction volumes; a downturn in any of these rapidly compresses both retail spend and agency commission revenue

Management explicitly flagged 'robust' competitive pressure with 'tactical sales practices' and 'below cost offers' in FY2026 filings, and commission-rate compression in livestock during periods of high stock prices
Strong wool sector remains structurally challenged by synthetic fibre competition despite a cyclical ~25% price recovery in H1 FY2026
Regional hail, cyclonic and wind events (Canterbury Plains, north-region cyclones) can disrupt arable, horticultural and irrigation-service operations

financial.risk: Rising net debt and working-capital seasonality
financial.description: Net interest-bearing debt rose to $170.7m at 31 Dec 2025 (from $106.7m a year earlier), partly funding the Nexan acquisition and seasonal H1 working-capital build (GO-STOCK receivables, inventory); H1 operating cash outflow was $49.9m
Syndicated core debt ($100m) and working-capital ($85m) facilities from BNZ, Rabobank and Westpac price off OCR/BKBM plus margin, so PGW's interest cost is directly exposed to NZ interest-rate moves
FY2025 NPAT margin of ~1.1% (FY2026 ~1.5%) leaves little buffer for cost inflation or a demand shock before profitability is impaired

regulatory.description: In October 2025 PGW briefly fell below the NZX Listing Rules minimum director/residency requirements following a shareholder-driven board ouster, forcing a trading halt -- evidence that large-shareholder actions can create real compliance risk
PGW has voluntarily continued NZ Climate Standards-aligned reporting even as proposed threshold changes may remove its mandatory climate-reporting entity status
Farmer customers face evolving on-farm environmental and freshwater regulation that can affect input spend and land-use decisions, an indirect but real risk to PGW's retail and real estate segments

macro.description: Fonterra's 2026/27 forecast was cut by 50c to $9.25/kgMS (range $8.00-$10.50) in July 2026 on softer global demand and rising supply -- a swing factor for dairy-related retail and real estate demand
A softer NZD benefits exporting customers' returns (positive for PGW indirectly) but raises the cost of imported agrichemical, animal health and equipment inputs PGW purchases

Management cited 'geopolitical risks' and noted recent China/India tariff reductions as a positive for wool market access -- underscoring sensitivity to shifts in trade policy for NZ's key export commodities
Management flagged weather, alongside commodity pricing, as one of the two key swing factors for the FY2027 result

macro_factors.industry_outlook: New Zealand's primary sector export revenue is forecast to reach a record $62.0 billion by 30 June 2026 (MPI), with dairy exports up ~1% to $27.4bn, red meat/wool up ~7% to $13.2bn, and horticulture up ~5% to $9.2bn -- a broadly supportive multi-year backdrop for PGW's rural retail and agency volumes after several difficult years
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- PGW's earnings (particularly the Agency segment) are tightly correlated with the on-farm profitability cycle: farmgate milk price, sheep/beef schedules, wool pricing and rural land values all move together with global commodity demand and NZ weather
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- direct exposure through floating-rate bank debt and lease liabilities, and indirect exposure through the effect of NZ interest rates on farmer confidence, rural property transactions and on-farm capital investment (e.g. irrigation)
key_input_costs: Agrichemicals and imported animal health products (FX-exposed)
Fertiliser (sold via distribution partnerships, e.g. Ballance)

recent_developments.event: FY2026 (year to 30 June 2026) full-year result: operating revenue $1,074m (+10%, first time above $1bn since the 2019 seeds divestment), Operating EBITDA $64.3m (+15%), NPAT $15.6m (+46%), EPS 20.6cps; final dividend 5.5cps fully imputed, taking FY2026 total dividend to 10cps
Fonterra cut its 2026/27 farmgate milk price forecast by 50c to $9.25/kgMS (range $8.00-$10.50) on softer global demand and rising supply, a headwind for dairy-linked demand into FY2027

H1 FY2026 result: operating revenue $619.4m (+9%), Operating EBITDA $45.7m (+11%), NPAT $17.3m (+8%); interim dividend 4.5cps fully imputed; net interest-bearing debt rose to $170.7m (from $106.7m a year earlier) partly funding the Nexan acquisition and seasonal working-capital build

Acquired Nexan Group, a New Zealand animal health manufacturer (Nexan and Vetmed brands) that PGW had partnered with for over a decade, for ~$19.7m cash, strengthening Agritrade's manufacturing/R&D capability
Launched Blue Ag, PGW's private-label agrichemical range, through Rural Supplies and Fruitfed Supplies stores, aimed at improving supply resilience and price-point control

Independent Chair Garry Moore and Deputy Chair Sarah Brown were voted out at the AShM by major shareholders Agria (~44%) and Elders (~12.3%) without stated reasons; the board briefly fell below NZX Listing Rule minimums (only 3 directors, 1 NZ-resident), triggering a same-day trading halt; John Nichol was appointed Independent Director/Chair the same day to restore compliance
Wilson Liu appointed Independent Director (became Audit Committee Chair from 14 October 2025)
Wool pricing recovered materially -- average strong wool prices up ~25% year-on-year on tightening supply and Chinese buying, though the sector remains structurally challenged long-term

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Full Year Result / H1 FY2026 Report

items.notes: This was the guidance reiterated at H1 FY2026 (Feb 2026) and delivered at the August 2026 full-year result

Management declined to give formal FY2027 numerical guidance at the August 2026 result, citing it as too early in the financial year; outlook characterised qualitatively as 'relatively strong' but dependent on commodity pricing and weather (potential El Nino). Detailed FY2027 update expected at the 30 October 2026 Annual Shareholders' Meeting following the spring trading period

items.target: 5.5 cps final (10.0 cps FY2026 total), fully imputed
items.notes: Interim dividend of 4.5cps was paid in H1 FY2026 (up from prior year); PGW has resumed a fully imputed progressive dividend as earnings recover from the FY2024 trough

guidance.management_commentary: Chair John Nichol and CEO Stephen Guerin's H1 FY2026 report described a 'generally supportive market environment' with favourable commodity pricing across dairy, red meat, wool, kiwifruit and apples, offset by weaker viticulture/arable demand. At the August 2026 full-year result, management flagged that FY2027 risk falls into two areas -- commodity pricing and weather (including potential El Nino) -- and that customer confidence and weather over the coming months will be the key determinants of the FY2027 outcome.

bull_case: Cyclical earnings recovery is well underway: FY2026 NPAT +46% and Operating EBITDA +15%, with revenue back above NZ$1bn for the first time since the 2019 seeds divestment, powered by strong livestock, red meat and dairy pricing
New Zealand's primary sector export revenue is forecast at a record $62bn for the year to June 2026, providing broad-based tailwinds to on-farm spending across PGW's retail and agency businesses
Vertical integration moves (Nexan acquisition, Blue Ag private label) should expand margins and differentiate PGW's offering versus pure distribution competitors
Progressive, fully imputed dividend has been resumed and increased (10cps FY2026) as earnings recover, offering income alongside cyclical upside
Rural real estate and livestock agency, PGW's highest-operating-leverage segments, are inflecting positively as lower interest rates and improved farm profitability reactivate buyer activity
bear_case: Ownership/governance overhang: Agria (~44%) and Elders (~12.3%) together control a majority and demonstrated willingness to abruptly remove independent directors, creating both strategic uncertainty and a brief NZX compliance breach in October 2025

Highly cyclical, thin-margin business (NPAT margin ~1-1.5%) with earnings tightly geared to volatile commodity prices (milk price, meat schedules, wool) that can reverse quickly -- Fonterra already cut its FY2027 milk price forecast in July 2026

Structurally sub-scale versus co-operative competitor Farmlands in rural retail, and facing explicitly 'robust'/'tactical' price competition and below-cost offers that pressure margins across the sector

Rising net debt ($170.7m at Dec 2025, up from $106.7m a year prior) funding both the Nexan acquisition and seasonal working capital, increasing floating-rate interest exposure just as the company re-levers for growth

Commission-rate compression in livestock agency during high-price periods (farmers push back on fees, use flat headage arrangements) means strong commodity prices do not translate one-for-one into PGW earnings growth
